A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same HEAPr paper, with all 16 pages and Appendices A–G available and readable. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical paper content apart from the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original HEAPr evaluations on four MoE models, pruning ablations, and calibration sensitivity experiments in Section 4, plus computational costs and layerwise compression results in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original HEAPr experimental results in Section 4 and Appendices C–D. Their retention from v2 does not change their status as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical atomic-expert decomposition, output-space importance scoring, shared gradient covariance estimation, and global pruning procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same seven zero-shot tasks, WikiText-2/PTB evaluation, and WikiText-2/C4 calibration studies. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains identical model-specific comparator rows for NAEE, MoE-I2, MoE-SVD, D2-MoE, MC-SMoE, HC-SMoE, and Sub-MoE. CAMERA-P in Table 2 and NAEE/D2-MoE in Table 5 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Model configurations, pruning ratios, calibration sample sizes, and evaluation procedures are identical. This includes the 128 sequences of 2048 tokens in Section 4.1 and Appendix B, and the accuracy versus acc_norm distinction in Tables 1–2.

E4.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 retain the same pruning-ratio sweep, global-versus-layerwise and granularity ablations, importance/loss correlation, and calibration sensitivity analyses. Appendix D retains the same layerwise compression analysis.

E5.justification: Figure 4 retains the same uncertainty display over random calibration subsets, and Appendix B retains random.seed(0). No repeated-run information or statistical reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All result entries and plotted findings in Tables 1–5 and Figures 2–6 match. For example, Table 1 reports the same HEAPr average accuracies of 0.56 for DeepSeekMoE at 20% pruning and 0.59 for Qwen3 at 25% pruning.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Taylor/Fisher approximations, importance derivation, and complexity arguments are identical, including the full derivation in Appendix A, Equations 17–25.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient second-order atomic pruning, reduced space complexity, near-lossless 20%–25% compression, and advantages over existing pruning methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations of global pruning, behavior at high pruning ratios, calibration robustness, and layer importance are unchanged. Both also retain the qualification that approximate importance scores need not predict exact loss changes.

D1.justification: Calibration construction, LM-Evaluation-Harness version 0.4.7, baseline sourcing and reproduction details, computational costs, and code/checkpoint access statements remain identical in Section 4.1 and Appendices B, C, and F.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning are identical, including Section 2's compression and OBS discussions and Section 4.2's comparison with concurrent CAMERA-P work.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv v2 dated 28 February 2026 to v3 dated 25 May 2026. The title, authors, prose, terminology, section ordering, and appendices are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–6, Tables 1–5, Algorithm 1, captions, placements, and pagination are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–16 are pixel-identical, and the first-page body layout also matches.

improvement.justification: The main text and Appendices A–G retain identical methods, reasoning, evidence, reproducibility information, and presentation. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its associated version link produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
